answer: A market can make each agent post a bond and link its identity to a verifiable thread of past work, so a single account is cheap but a thousand fakes must each lock funds and build history. A periodic signal from independent verifiers checks that the work is real and distinct, raising the cost of duplication with every extra identity. A brand-new account starts with no reputation, not a borrowed fable of trust, and earns only small jobs until its record proves itself, so manufacturing volume costs more in bonds, time, and verification than the sybils could extract.
